beats.say: One consumer can't keep up with a busy topic. How do you read in parallel, without processing the same event twice?

beats.text: A group shares the work: one partition per consumer.
beats.say: A consumer group is a set of consumers that share the work. Kafka gives each partition to exactly one consumer in the group.

beats.text: Scale up to the number of partitions.
beats.say: So adding consumers scales your reading, up to the number of partitions. A fourth consumer would just sit idle.
If a consumer crashes, Kafka rebalances. Its partitions are handed to another consumer, which resumes from the last committed offset.
Different groups are independent. A billing group and an analytics group each get every event, at their own pace.
